The chevron survives in `secondaryAction` and flips between chevron_up_20_regular and chevron_down_20_regular with field focus, which is the closest signal this widget exposes to upstream's `open`.

components-tagpicker--single-select.why: Single selection is the caller's job: onChanged keeps only `values.last`, so the picker never shows a second chip.

components-tagpicker--size.why: Upstream's `<h4>` headings become Text in typography.subtitle2 above each picker; the three sizes map onto FluentTagPickerSize.extraLarge/large/medium.

components-tagpicker--truncated-text.why: The CSS pair (text-overflow: ellipsis on the container, plus a 50px fixed width) becomes TextOverflow.ellipsis under an explicit ConstrainedBox — a tag lays its content out in an unbounded Row, so Text alone would never truncate. The container-width case is bounded at 240.

components-teachingpopover--carousel.why: Upstream declares three TeachingPopoverCarouselCards and lets TeachingPopoverCarousel page between them. FluentTeachingPopover shows one body at a time with FluentTeachingPopoverCarousel(steps/activeStep/onStepSelected) driving the dot strip, so the three cards became a `_pages` list indexed by `_step`. TeachingPopoverCarouselFooter's next/previous/initialStepText/finalStepText became the two footer buttons' labels ('Next'/'Finish', 'Previous'/'Close'); TeachingPopoverCarouselNavButton's `aria-label={`Tip ${index}`}` became `stepSemanticLabel`.

components-teachingpopover--carousel-bra.why: Same card-list-to-step adaptation as Carousel, with appearance: FluentTeachingPopoverAppearance.brand.

components-teachingpopover--carousel-tex.why: Upstream replaces the nav dots with TeachingPopoverCarouselPageCount rendering `${currentIndex} of ${totalPages}`. FluentTeachingPopoverCarousel draws its `pageCount` widget beside the dot strip rather than instead of it, so this footer shows both the dots and '1 of 3'. Noted in a comment inside the docregion.

components-teachingpopover--default.why: FluentTeachingPopover is controlled (required `open` + `onOpenChanged`), so the demo owns a `_open` bool and the 'TeachingPopover trigger' FluentButton toggles it. Upstream's TeachingPopoverTrigger/Surface/Header/Body/Title/Footer slot tree collapses into the widget's `child`/`header`/`media`/`title`/`body`/`primaryAction`/`secondaryAction` parameters; `onDismiss: () {}` is what draws the header's dismiss button.

components-textarea--appearance.why: griffel classes (inverted background wrapper, inverted label colour, mNudge padding) become Container/Padding with FluentSpacing.mNudge and colors.neutralBackgroundInverted / neutralForegroundInverted2; upstream's resize="both" has no counterpart.

components-textarea--controlled.why: FluentTextarea is controller-driven rather than value/onChange-driven, so the demo owns a TextEditingController seeded with 'initial value' and the 50-character cap is enforced by maxLength: 50 instead of rejecting the edit inside onChange.

components-textarea--resize.why: resize toggles the browser's native drag grip on <textarea>. Flutter has no such affordance, so 'none'/'horizontal' pin the height with maxLines: 2 and 'vertical'/'both' keep the default maxLines: null so the field grows with its text.

components-textarea--size.why: React's Field passes size down to the control through FieldContext; FluentField sizes only its own label, so size is set on both FluentField and FluentTextarea to match the rendering.

components-textarea--uncontrolled.why: console.log becomes debugPrint, keeping the 'New value: "..."' format and the 'Check console for new value' hint.

components-toast--default.why: Upstream hangs `action` off ToastTitle and wraps content in Toast/ToastTitle/ToastBody/ToastFooter children. FluentToast is one widget with named slots, so the Undo link goes in `action` with `type: FluentToastType.action`, and body/subtitle/footer are parameters.

components-toast--default-toast-options.why: position, timeout and pauseOnHover are arguments to FluentToastController.show rather than props on FluentToaster, so 'defaults configured on the Toaster' become three constants the demo passes at dispatch. `pauseOnWindowBlur` has no equivalent at all — the countdown keeps running when the window loses focus.

components-toast--dismiss-toast.why: No `onStatusChange`. FluentToastController is a ChangeNotifier, so the Make/Dismiss button state is derived by listening to the queue and checking whether the id is still in `entries`.

components-toast--dismiss-toast-with-act.why: There is no ToastTrigger. FluentToastBuilder is handed the toast's own id, so the link calls controller.dismiss(id) directly.

components-toast--focus-keyboard-shortcu.why: FluentToaster exposes no `shortcuts` slot. The focus move to the most recent toast is implemented (a FocusNode inside each dispatched toast), but binding it to CTRL+M needs LogicalKeyboardKey from package:flutter/services.dart, which these pages may not import, so it is offered as a second button. Upstream also pauses every toast in the toaster once one is focused; ours pauses on hover only.

components-toast--inline.why: FluentToaster always renders into the nearest Overlay, so `inline` is not a flag — it is a nearer overlay. Overlay.wrap gives the 500x500 box one of its own and the toasts stack inside it. Upstream's 2px dashed green border is solid here; BoxDecoration has no dash pattern.

components-toast--intent.why: There is no `media` slot on the title. A custom spinner or avatar goes in FluentToast's `icon`, paired with FluentToastIntent.custom — the one intent that ships no glyph of its own to replace.

components-toast--inverted-appearance.why: FluentToast has no `appearance` axis. The inverted surface is composed by passing the two tokens upstream's inverted rule names — neutralBackgroundStatic and neutralForegroundStaticInverted — through `style`, with the links switched to FluentLinkAppearance.overBrand.

components-toast--multiple-toasters.why: Upstream needs a toasterId because the DOM gives it no other handle on a particular toaster. A FluentToastController IS the handle, so two toasters are two controllers and two nested FluentToasters, and the per-toaster position is passed at dispatch.

components-toast--pause-and-play.why: There is no pauseToast/playToast pair. Re-showing under the same id with Duration.zero stops the countdown ticker and re-showing with the original timeout resumes it from where it stopped, which is exactly upstream's pause/play. The ToggleButton is a FluentButton wearing the primary appearance while checked, since fluent_2 ships no toggle button.

components-toast--pause-on-window-blur.why: FluentToastController.show has no pauseOnWindowBlur and the countdown is a ticker on the scheduler's clock, so it keeps running while another window has focus. The toast is upstream's; the pause is not.

components-toast--progress-toast.why: The 100ms/5-step interval is a TweenAnimationBuilder over the same wall-clock run — these pages may not import dart:async for a Timer — and ToastTrigger is replaced by a link that dismisses by id. Dismissal is still driven by the bar's own completion callback, as upstream intends.

components-toast--toast-lifecycle.why: No onStatusChange hook. The status is derived from the queue: present+visible, present+not-visible and absent give visible/dismissed/unmounted. `queued` is not observable, because our controller renders every toast it is given rather than holding a limit and a queue behind it.

components-toast--toaster-limit.why: FluentToaster has no `limit` and no queue behind one. The demo dismisses the oldest visible toast once the limit is exceeded — dropped rather than queued, which is the nearest the public API expresses.

components-toast--update-toast.why: No updateToast; `show` with an id already queued replaces that toast in place and keeps its slot, which is the same operation. The unmounted flag is again derived from the queue rather than from onStatusChange.

components-toolbar--controlled-radio.why: Same composition as Radio; upstream's checkedValues/onCheckedValueChange round trip becomes local setState.

components-toolbar--controlled-toggle-bu.why: Upstream's controlled/uncontrolled split is a React prop pair (checkedValues + onCheckedValueChange). In Flutter the demo already owns the state, so the round trip is written out as a Map<String, Set<String>> plus setState, seeded with textOptions: bold, italic.

components-toolbar--far-group.why: Upstream is one Toolbar with justifyContent: space-between and two ToolbarGroups. FluentToolbar hugs its content (Row with mainAxisSize.min) and has no group widget, so the two groups are two FluentToolbars pushed apart by a spaceBetween Row, wrapped in one Semantics container carrying the 'with Separeted Groups' label.

components-toolbar--overflow-items.why: FluentToolbar models no overflow — buildFluentToolbar is a Row with mainAxisSize.min and the widget documents 'supply your own overflow menu as the last item'. There is no Flutter equivalent of upstream's Overflow/useIsOverflowItemVisible measurement, so every button stays visible and the trailing 'More items' FluentMenu lists the same commands in upstream's three divider-separated groups.

components-toolbar--radio.why: No FluentToolbarRadioGroup/RadioButton exists. Single-select is a Map<String, String> of one checked value per group name, rendered as FluentButtons re-resolved with WidgetState.selected.

components-toolbar--subtle.why: No FluentToolbarToggleButton exists; the toggle is a FluentButton re-resolved with WidgetState.selected folded in.

components-toolbar--transparent.why: No FluentToolbarToggleButton exists; the toggle is a FluentButton (appearance transparent) re-resolved with WidgetState.selected folded in.

components-toolbar--vertical.why: FluentToolbar has no vertical axis — buildFluentToolbar lays items out in a Row, and nesting a Column inside one item would collapse the three buttons into a single roving-focus stop. Rendered as a Semantics-labelled Column of the same buttons, each keeping its own tab stop.

components-toolbar--vertical-button.why: FluentButton.iconPosition is before/after only. The vertical button is built as the button's label — an icon stacked over the text — and because the icon slot is what carries the button's foreground colour, the stacked glyph reads that colour from the button's own resolved style at rest (tracks the theme, not hover).

components-toolbar--with-tooltip.why: fluent_2 ships no toggle button. Each ToolbarToggleButton is a FluentButton whose style is the button's own, re-resolved with WidgetState.selected folded into the live interaction states — the state Fluent's *Selected tokens key on — so hover, press and disabled still win.

components-tooltip--controlled.why: FluentTooltip owns its own hover/focus tracking and exposes no visible/onVisibleChange; the checkbox drives enabled, which is the gate upstream's `visible && enabled` actually demonstrates.

components-tooltip--custom-mount.why: No mountNode. FluentTooltip calls Overlay.of, so the demo wraps the trigger in a local Overlay — the nearest Overlay is Flutter's portal host.

components-tooltip--icon.why: FluentInfoLabel requires infoSemanticLabel outright (React derives the info button's name from the label it is wired to); the upstream Link is a callback because this package depends on no URL launcher.

components-tooltip--overflow-hidden.why: The surface lives in the nearest Overlay, above the scroll view and unclipped by it, so the tip does not hide when the trigger scrolls away — FluentTooltip has no clip-boundary parameter. Layout and copy kept; gap named in the docregion.

components-tooltip--positioning.why: FluentTooltipPosition has four sides and no start/end alignment axis, so the four supported placements render and the eight aligned variants are dropped rather than faked.

components-tooltip--relationship-descrip.why: No relationship axis; FluentTooltip.semanticLabel is announced alongside the trigger's own name, which is what aria-describedby provides.

components-tooltip--relationship-label.why: React's relationship="label" writes the tooltip text into the trigger's aria-label; FluentTooltip has no relationship axis, so the same string is passed to FluentButton.icon's required semanticLabel.

components-tooltip--styled.why: griffel className on the content slot has no Flutter equivalent; the same two tokens (brandBackground, neutralForegroundInverted) go through FluentTooltipStyle.

components-tooltip--target.why: No positioning.target. A FluentTooltip always anchors to its own child, so the button's icon slot is what gets wrapped and the surface points at the icon.

components-tree--actions.why: FluentMenu opens from its own trigger and has no openOnContext, so the row keeps the edit button and the overflow menu and drops the duplicate context menu; FluentTreeItem also has no aria-description equivalent.

components-tree--appearance.why: TreeItemPersonaLayout's media slot becomes FluentTreeItem.icon holding a FluentAvatar; Avatar color="colorful" has no counterpart, so a palette family and explicit initials are named per avatar because FluentAvatar deliberately does not derive initials from name. The aria-labels ride on Semantics wrappers.

components-tree--aside.why: FluentTreeItem has one trailing slot (actions) where upstream has two that share a spot (aside/actions); CounterBadge maps to a small danger FluentBadge; the row has no description field, so upstream's aria-description is passed to the aside and announced with it.

components-tree--customizing-interaction.why: A FluentTree row is one hit target, so onOpenChange cannot distinguish a content click from a chevron click the way data.type does; the row both opens and reports through onInvoke, and Flutter has no alert() so the message renders under the tree.

components-tree--drag-and-drop.why: No dnd-kit and no sortable-list primitive in package:flutter/widgets; the same eight items are reordered from the row's trailing actions so the story — a tree whose leaves can be rearranged — still works.

components-tree--expand-icon.why: FluentTree draws its own chevron and exposes no expandIcon slot, so the AddSquare16Regular/SubtractSquare16Regular pair goes in the leading icon slot and tracks the same controlled openItems set.

components-tree--flat-tree.why: There is no FlatTree; the same items are nested and aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset and parentValue all fall out of the structure instead of being supplied by hand.

components-tree--icon-before-and-after.why: iconBefore is FluentTreeItem.icon; iconAfter has no counterpart, so it uses the trailing actions slot, which sits at the end of the row rather than immediately after the label.

components-tree--infinite-scrolling.why: A Future and a ScrollNotification stand in for the Promise and the onScroll handler; FluentTree lays its rows out as a column, so the 400px container is a SingleChildScrollView rather than an overflowing tree.

components-tree--inline-styling-tree-ite.why: Upstream recurses through useSubtreeContext_unstable for arbitrary depth; FluentTree derives the level from a data tree, so the depth is materialised at twelve levels and the per-level inset is set once through FluentTreeItemStyle.indent.

components-tree--layouts.why: TreeItemPersonaLayout maps to a FluentPersona label, which composes avatar, primary and description lines. "without media" is FluentPersona(presenceOnly: true) with no status, whose media slot resolves to nothing.

components-tree--lazy-loading.why: The captured story references a mockFetch helper it does not include, so no upstream row names exist; the loaded rows are numbered from the branch value rather than invented. The shape — open, spinner in the expand slot, live-region announcements — is upstream's.

components-tree--manipulation.why: Add and remove are written against two flat subtrees as upstream does, but FluentTree owns focus and moves it to the next visible row itself, so the itemToFocusRef bookkeeping is unnecessary.

components-tree--motion-custom.why: FluentTree exposes no collapseMotion hook, so the duration slider and the animate-opacity switch are live and the collapse animation is not; avatarless personas keep the neutral fill because color="colorful" has no counterpart.

components-tree--navigation-mode-tree-gr.why: FluentTree has a single navigation model — arrow keys walk visible rows, Tab reaches the actions — and no navigationMode field, so the composition is identical to Actions and only the keyboard route differs.

components-tree--open-item-controlled.why: FluentTree owns the open set for the whole tree; there is no per-item open prop, so the whole set is controlled and 'tree-item-1' starts inside it.

components-tree--selection.why: FluentTree always takes selectedItems from the caller, so defaultCheckedItems ['1-2'] becomes the initial value of local state.

components-tree--use-headless-flat-tree.why: No useHeadlessFlatTree hook: the flat value/parentValue list is kept verbatim (it is what the story is about) and folded into nested items by a local helper; the per-row context menu is dropped for the same reason as Actions.

components-tree--virtualization.why: No react-window equivalent, and Flutter's widgets layer has no drop-in virtualiser for a component that lays itself out as a column; FluentTree already builds only the rows its open set makes visible, so the 600 items are real and the 300x300 viewport just scrolls them.
